text:
ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) - A Georgia urologist is speaking out about erectile dysfunction clinics after a local patient paid $11,500 for treatments that are available elsewhere for hundreds of dollars.

Dr. Charles Kaplan, a urologist at Georgia Urology, reviewed an Atlanta News First investigation into a patient who paid an ED clinic thousands of dollars, received one free treatment, and tried to cancel, but the clinic stopped responding to him.

“It was unfortunate what happened to the man, but it’s not uncommon,” Dr. Kaplan said.

Calvin Pauling, 74, went to Priority Men’s Medical Center in Dunwoody after hearing a radio advertisement promising a free consultation and first treatment.

Pauling said he experienced what felt like a sales pitch. His free treatment included an injection. After the treatment, Pauling met with an associate who presented a no-refunds contract totaling $11,500. Pauling said the associate helped him apply for a credit card to pay for the treatments.

Dr. Kaplan said injection therapy does work and has been around for decades, but that’s not where patients should start.

“I’ve seen patients who have gone to men’s health clinics who’ve never even tried an oral medication before,” he said. “They just get started with an injection therapy, and that’s not normally how we do it. We always start with the least invasive treatment.”

Dr. Kaplan recently met with a patient who paid an ED clinic $15,000. He started a blog about ED clinics and offered advice for men experiencing erectile dysfunction.

“If you’re having problems with erectile dysfunction, your first step is to go to your family doctor, your primary care doctor, and start there,” he said. “These men’s health clinics are never going to offer you oral medications like Viagra, because they don’t make any money on those drugs.”

After the investigation, a Priority spokesman said a refund for treatments not received was “100 percent reasonable.”

But Pauling said he never received it. Priority Men’s Medical Center and its parent company, Stratford Medical Group in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, have not responded to multiple requests for comment.

Pauling disputed the charges for services he did not receive.
